messages:
mike: Heads up — saw a p50 latency regression on small-seq requests after yesterday's kernel autotune rollout. Short contexts (~<32 tokens) are being routed to the AVX fused "heavy" kernel instead of the lightweight short-path. :thinking:

sanjay: Noted. Do we have traces or profiler dumps? Curious if this is a routing misclassification or a kernel perf regression.

mike: Quick numbers from canary cluster (last 30m):
- median seq len: 24
- p50 latency: 21ms -> 48ms
- p95 latency: 120ms -> 240ms

Attached execution snippet from perftools: 
```
kernel_choice: avx_fused_attention
seq_len: 24
batch_size: 8
exec_time_us: 43000
kv_cache_hits: 76
kv_cache_misses: 12
batching_efficiency: 0.62
```

anna: That exec_time smells like prefill work hitting the decode-optimized kernel, causing poor microcache locality. The autotuner might be using average seq len to pick kernel for the entire bucket.

julia: Our autotune objective currently favors throughput. For short-context interactive workloads we should bias towards latency-optimal picks even if throughput drops a bit.

kevin: @mike can you run the seq-hist helper? `/infra/scripts/seq_hist.sh --since 30m --model redwood-v2` to dump live bucket counts.

mike: ran it, output: 
```
[0-16): 34%
[16-64): 45%
[64-128): 12%
[128+): 9%
current_bucket_boundaries: [16,64,128]
autotune_pick: avx_fused_attention for [16-64)
```

sanjay: There it is. The autotuner picked avx_fused for [16-64) because the tail (64 tokens) pushed the mean up. But majority of requests are ~20 tokens. We need a short-path override or hysteresis so we don't flip on short-lived tail effects.

ops-oncall: Routing shows ~40% of requests in that bucket are being served by the heavy kernel. Can we patch routing to prefer the light kernel when batch mean <= 32 until autotuner reevaluates?

anna: Quick mitigation proposal: add a per-bucket runtime override: if mean_seq_in_batch <= 32 and batch_size <= 16 -> prefer light_kernel. It's a reversible, low-risk change.

kevin: I can canary that to cluster-3. Rollout command: 
```
rbctl route set --cluster cluster-3 --model redwood-v2 --bucket "16-64" --prefer light_kernel --ttl 15m
```

mike: Do it. Also add a `kernel_decision_reason` tag (tuner|override|default) to logs so we can correlate decisions with perf.

infra-bot: deploy queued: rbctl job 90412. Canary target: cluster-3. Will post when live. :gear:

julia: Longer-term: change autotune objective to include a latency penalty for buckets where >60% requests < 32 tokens. Also require hysteresis (e.g., 5% sustained improvement over 10 minutes) before flipping kernel picks.

sanjay: I'll open a lightweight RFC + autotune config PR and include a replayable perf harness for short-ctx traces.

mike: Canary applied — monitoring p50/p95 and kv cache metrics.

kevin: Canary live (rbctl job 90412 started at 1800501350). Logging tag enabled.

mike: First 5m after canary:
- p50: 22ms (back to baseline)
- p95: 130ms
- routing: 92% short requests -> light_kernel
- kv_cache_miss_rate: stable

mike: Looks promising. Keeping canary 30m before decide promote.

ops-oncall: Mitigation documented in runbook INF-3287. Rollback condition: p95 > 20% above baseline.

julia: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/142-kernel-autotune-shortctx

sanjay: Will post PR once we validate canary stability; will attach flamegraphs and microbench traces.

mike: Will close loop after 1h and attach flamegraphs to RFC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
